# Common relational structure for multivalued joining

<!-- Generated by tools/research/registry.py; edit the matching JSON record. -->

`multivalued-joining-common-structure` · **recorded-checked** · theorem · F22 · [record](multivalued-joining-common-structure.json) · [register](../../../../RESULTS.md)

> Two descriptions of a joining with one kernel that is a bisimulation lift it, align one to one on used codes and carry its reading across; where pairs join into listed fragments, codes whose kernel is sameness of branching tests suffice under excluded middle, and the relation can stay multivalued.

<a id="laws--规律"></a>
## Laws

1. A joining relates two fragments to what they join into, in several ways, one or none. Read as a frame, a fragment moves, with a partner on either side, to what they join into; the bisimulations of that frame are exactly the relations compatible with the joining: related fragments joined with one partner on one side give related results, either way. (`Becoming.Joining.frame`, `Becoming.Joining.Compatible`, `Becoming.Joining.bisimulation_iff_compatible`)
   - *Shared laws, by Lean dependency:* no shared law's anchor among the constants its declarations use.
2. Read through a description, codes join where fragments with those codes join. For any joining, the description lifts it, every joining of codes coming from a joining of the fragments themselves, exactly where having one code is a bisimulation of the joining's frame, with no premise; where it lifts, a joining of codes is exactly the code of a joining of any fragments having them. (`Becoming.Joining.image`, `Becoming.Joining.Lifts`, `Becoming.Joining.lifts_iff`, `Becoming.Joining.image_iff`)
   - *Shared laws, by Lean dependency:* no shared law's anchor among the constants its declarations use.
3. For any joining, two descriptions with one kernel that is a bisimulation of the joining's frame each lift the joining, are aligned one to one on the codes they use (each used code with exactly one code of the other, through a fragment having both), and the alignment carries one reading of the joining onto the other, with no further premise. (`Becoming.Used`, `Becoming.Aligned`, `Becoming.aligned_one_to_one`, `Becoming.Joining.common_structure`)
   - *Shared laws, by Lean dependency:* no shared law's anchor among the constants its declarations use.
4. Under excluded middle, for a joining whose pairs each join into listed fragments, fragments are alike exactly where they pass the same branching tests, and two descriptions whose codes identify exactly the fragments passing the same branching tests each lift the joining, align one to one on used codes, and carry one reading onto the other; the joining may have several outcomes. (`Becoming.Joining.FiniteOutcomes`, `Becoming.Joining.FiniteOutcomes.alike_iff_sameBranchingTests`, `Becoming.Joining.FiniteOutcomes.common_structure`)
   - *Shared laws, by Lean dependency:* no shared law's anchor among the constants its declarations use.
5. Under excluded middle, for a joining whose pairs each join into listed fragments, fragments passing the same branching tests join into fragments passing the same tests, and a presentation reading the branching tests exactly and reducedly lifts the joining; for any two frames that list each move's outcomes, passing the same branching tests is a bisimulation. (`Becoming.Joining.FiniteOutcomes.joined_sameBranchingTests_of_em`, `Becoming.Joining.FiniteOutcomes.lifts_of_exact`, `Becoming.SameBranchingTests.bisimulation_of_em`)
   - *Shared laws, by Lean dependency:* no shared law's anchor among the constants its declarations use.
6. For any configurations and questions, a presentation is exact where each configuration's code reads its answers, and reduced where configurations answering alike get one code. An exact reduced presentation gives one code exactly to configurations answering alike, and two exact reduced presentations correspond one to one on used codes. (`Becoming.Presentations.Exact`, `Becoming.Presentations.Reduced`, `Becoming.Presentations.reduced_exact_kernel`, `Becoming.Presentations.relative_unique_correspondence`)
   - *Shared laws, by Lean dependency:* no shared law's anchor among the constants its declarations use.
7. Where predicates on the questions answering alike are one predicate, every exact presentation factors through the canonical one, which codes each configuration by the predicate of its answers: each used code matches exactly one used canonical code and each used canonical code is matched; on a frame, the canonical codes of two configurations are one exactly where they pass the same branching tests. (`Becoming.Presentations.PredicateExt`, `Becoming.Presentations.canonical_factor`, `Becoming.PresentationFrames.canonical_kernel`)
   - *Shared laws, by Lean dependency:* no shared law's anchor among the constants its declarations use.
8. For an exact reduced presentation, a three-place relation on configurations descends to an exact reading on codes exactly where it is the same for configurations answering alike, its image then being that reading; any two exact readings agree on used codes; and for a reduced presentation, one pair of triples answering alike on which the relation differs blocks every exact reading. (`Becoming.Presentations.Saturated`, `Becoming.Presentations.RelExact`, `Becoming.Presentations.relation_descends_iff_saturated`, `Becoming.Presentations.lift_exact_iff_saturated`, `Becoming.Presentations.relational_reading_unique_on_used`, `Becoming.Presentations.separating_relation_blocks_descent`)
   - *Shared laws, by Lean dependency:* no shared law's anchor among the constants its declarations use.
9. In the periphery (propext, Quot.sound), in a finite joining where split joined with enter gives the two outcomes leftOnly and rightOnly, the joining read through the canonical presentation is not functional: the common relation can stay multivalued. (`Generative.ExplanatoryJoiningBranchWitnesses.canonical_operation_still_multivalued`)
   - *Shared laws, by Lean dependency:* not measured: none of its declarations is in the spine run the measure reads.

<a id="conditions--条件"></a>
## Conditions

- One partial joining relation J; for the finite-outcome laws, each input pair joins into a listed, finite set of fragments.
- The target contains all finite negation, conjunction and left/right joining-successor questions, with no independent atomic predicates.
- Exact supplies complete truthful answers; Reduced is used for minimal codes and lifting output codes.
- Excluded middle is a named hypothesis of the finite-outcome laws: where outcomes are listed, it matches the steps of fragments passing the same branching tests, and so identifies that sameness with likeness; with the kernel supplied as a bisimulation, the laws use no premise beyond the two named.

<a id="does-not-show--未表明"></a>
## Does not show

- The alignment carries the joining read on codes, its outcome classes, not every joining fact among the fragments themselves.
- That a given explanation's description is exact and reduced, and a common correspondence across articulations into different fragments, do not follow.
- **Counterexample:** One law has distinguishable left/right outcomes; the canonical presentation remains nonfunctional, and shared continuation differs from individually feasible paths. [source](../../../../experiments/integrated-correction/general-framework/generative-basis/lean/deeper/ExplanatoryJoiningBranchWitnesses.lean)

**Standard boundaries:** No ethical premise is used. The core declarations use no Lean axiom; the periphery declarations cited use only Lean's standard axioms (propext, Quot.sound, Classical.choice), as their receipts report. · Uses decidability of the named determinations, a logical commitment written as a hypothesis.
